This game is borderline brilliant.  It's like someone made 85% of a masterpiece, and then stopped.  Thumbs down because of a few major issues that take it from being one of the greatest games I've ever seen all the way down to just not being worth $3.99, unfortunately.

First of all, the art is great (although you'll see the same handful of characters over and over), the gameplay idea is good, and the actual gameplay of turn-based sword fighting is well done.  The problems include a complete lack of balance.  Pretty early on (think less than half through the game) you will get to a point where you just one-shot every enemy before they can even act.  This includes bosses, and the final boss.  From mid-game on there is just no reason to play other than to see what happens (it's not a ton, just FYI).  

Not only are the fights meaningless for most of the game, but you also see the same random events over, and over... and over.  I think I killed the same escaping criminal 5 times, heard the same old man story from 4 different old guys, same lady ghost on a bridge 3 times, same couple on a bridge 3 times, etc.  This is in one play through.  I completed the master sword thing, ran into another of the blacksmiths and asked for a sword and he gave me the same sword to upgrade again, and on and on.

There are items and special swords to take from the masters and such, but there is nowhere to sell them (the merchants don't have the money to buy most of your loot), and there is nothing meaningful to buy anyway.  I was just donating hundreds at temples and buying most expensive foods and geisha because, why not?  You one-shot every enemy, so there is no need for healing or anything.

Anyway, it's $3.99 so it's tough to go wrong if you want to check out the well done sword fighting and the art and such, but after you "get" it, just know that the game itself isn't very good (and it could have been great).

This game deserves WAY more attention and recognition than it has.

Basically it's a rogue-lite duelling simulator with heavy accent on atmosphere of feudal Japan. All visuals are done with actual historical artwork and game has an amazing attention to detail when it comes to historical atmosphere, with small jokes and references all over the place. The tone is not overly serious, but not a complete punchline-fest. 
The fighting system itself is amazing for how simple this game is. There are a LOT of ways to build a character, and while grinding xp is useful, it isn't necessary, which makes low-xp "pacifist" runs particularly interesting, since you WILL have to fight eventually and will have to make the most of what you have at that point.

The main con of the game is lack of content. There are very few encounters for each map node type, and you learn them all pretty quickly. Even so, game has a lot of weird specific interactions to find, which, combined with a lot of different starting characters and builds, makes it really replayable.

Also, even with pretty simple dialog system, this game has better roleplay than many modern RPGs.

All in all, extremely glad I stumbled upon this gem, highly recommended, especially if you like feudal japan setting or weird indie rogue-likes in general.
